domains.angle: Adverse-event and provider registries link back to device/drug identifiers already coming in from Pharma.
Deep FDA bench — UNII/510k/PMA/MAUDE/FAERS all key off the same establishment and product IDs.
The deepest bench here — TRI/RCRA/AQS/GHGRP all key off facility IDs, so one polluter shows up everywhere at once.
Cross with corporate registration to catch a bank/thrift still chartered after enforcement action elsewhere.
MIC/MPID/PCAOB data is thin but real — mostly identifier scaffolding, not incident data.
Sanctions/PSC/offshore data is the AML backbone — pairs directly with Corporate Registration for shell-company chains.
Beneficial-ownership layer for the entity spine — trace who actually sits behind a sanctioned or offshore shell.
NLRB case data ties labor complaints to the same employer entity seen in procurement/corporate data.
Federal judge/case metadata to connect enforcement outcomes back to the people who ruled on them.
Sentencing and detention facility data — mostly state-fragmented, so coverage will always be partial without 50 state builds.
ICE detention data is large and sensitive — pairs with facility/contractor data to map who profits from detention.
Lobbyist/political-filer data lets you connect money in politics to the same entities showing up in enforcement or procurement.
Carrier and accident IDs support incident-to-operator resolution once paired with FAA registration data.
Thinnest realm — only one clean bulk source; most of this domain is scrape-only or fragmented.
Chain device/drug recalls (MAUDE, 510k, enforcement) to the same manufacturer across FDA and CPSC surfaces.
OPEID/IPEDS crosswalk to tie predatory-lending or fraud patterns to a specific accredited institution.
Best-covered realm — HMDA, FHA, Ginnie Mae, CFPB complaints all key on lender ID, ready for a full redlining/predatory-lending pass.
Audit and award data flags who's getting federal money while under separate enforcement elsewhere.
Plant/utility/generator IDs let pollution and safety incidents resolve to one owner across EIA + EPA.
Nothing survived the critic pass clean — every checked row downgraded; treat this realm as unconfirmed.
Almost nothing survived the critic pass — FCC/USAC portals are search tools, not files; treat this realm as effectively unmapped.
Almost entirely state-fragmented — one national source (Canada OSFI) confirmed, everything else needs a state-by-state build.
Thin, but OPEID ties student-aid harm to the same institutions surfaced in Education.
Cleanest realm in the whole sweep — DOI/ORCID/ROR/grant IDs make researcher and funder identity resolution nearly solved.
The connective tissue for cross-border ownership — SIREN, GLEIF, OpenSanctions bridge US entities to foreign registries.
